raw_response:
Aiya, the growing season again. Let me think through it the way I always do — I've been working this land for 53 years, I know what it wants.

My 20 mu sits between the village and the road. Six mu in the western strip I keep in cotton, that's the ground my father planted cotton on and it's still good for it — the soil is a bit sandy there, drains well. The other 14 mu I do wheat then maize, same as most people around here. Every year the same.

**For the wheat** — I already put it in back in October, so now I'm just thinking about how to bring it through. Before I planted I spread two bags of the compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind the shop sells) per mu, worked it in with the tractor the neighbor runs for us. Cost me maybe 300 yuan a mu just for that, plus the seed I saved from last year's harvest — I don't buy seed for wheat, waste of money, my wheat has always come up fine. Now at green-up in March I'll put down one bag of urea per mu, maybe a bit more if the leaves look yellow. My neighbor Old Wang, he puts down more, but his field is thinner soil. Mine doesn't need as much.

Irrigation — I'll run the well three times if the sky is dry. Before winter once, at green-up once, at filling once. Each time costs me electricity and the pump, maybe 40 yuan a mu. If it rains good in spring I skip one. Last year I only irrigated twice and got 420 jin per mu, not bad. I expect about the same.

**For the maize** — right after I cut the wheat in June, no time to rest. Same 14 mu. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, you have to, the old seed doesn't work for maize. I use the Zhengdan variety my son-in-law told me about, the shop has it. Plant it straight into the wheat stubble with the hired planter, no tillage, no time. One bag of compound per mu at planting, then when it's knee-high I side-dress one bag of urea. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — if the rains come I don't irrigate at all, if July is dry I give it one shot at tasseling. Usually I get 450 jin a mu. Sometimes more, sometimes less, depends on the sky.

**For the cotton** — 6 mu on the western strip. Planted late April after the soil warms. I use the seed the co-op gives, about 40 yuan a mu. Cotton takes work, not so much money on fertilizer but lots of hands. One bag of compound before planting, then I break urea into two topdressings — once at budding, once at flowering. Maybe half a bag each time. Pesticide yes — bollworm, aphid, mites, cotton gets everything. I spray four or five times through the summer. It's expensive but you can't skip or you lose the whole bole. My wife and I and when the kids come back on weekends do the picking September into October. Three or four pickings, back breaking. I expect maybe 250 jin of seed cotton per mu if the weather holds.

Money is tight. Two of my sons work at the factory in Handan and send something, but I don't count on it. I keep enough cash aside for one emergency — if a pump breaks, if someone gets sick. I don't borrow for fertilizer. If I can't afford the full amount I just put down less. My father always said: don't go into debt for the fields, the fields owe you, you don't owe them.
